title: Here’s Why Dreams During Naps Are So Weird
summary:
遇到创作瓶颈时，托马斯·爱迪生常通过打盹来寻找突破。这位发明家会手握一枚沉重的钢球，靠在座位上打瞌睡，刚滑入梦乡之际，钢球落地便将他唤醒。此后，无论是科学研究还是人们的经验轶事，都为爱迪生这种“打盹策略”提供了支持，表明当人处在清醒与入睡之间的“朦胧地带”时，大脑能够碰撞出全新的思维联想。而如今，发表在《细胞报告》上的一项最新研究指出，即便在清醒状态下，人们也有可能进入这种类似梦境的状态。

来源：Nautilus；作者：Jake Currie；原文发布时间：2026-05-04 20:05:00

paragraphs.contentEn: Thomas Edison used to break through creative blocks by napping. The inventor would settle in with a heavy steel ball in one hand, doze off, and awaken when it fell, just after dipping his toes into slumberland. Since then, both scientific research and anecdotal reports have supported Edison’s nap strategy, demonstrating that our brains can make novel connections when we slip into the “twilight zone” between sleep and wakefulness. Now, new research published in Cell Reports suggests we can access these dream-like states when we’re awake, too.
paragraphs.contentZh: 遇到创作瓶颈时，托马斯·爱迪生常通过打盹来寻找突破。这位发明家会手握一枚沉重的钢球，靠在座位上打瞌睡，刚滑入梦乡之际，钢球落地便将他唤醒。此后，无论是科学研究还是人们的经验轶事，都为爱迪生这种“打盹策略”提供了支持，表明当人处在清醒与入睡之间的“朦胧地带”时，大脑能够碰撞出全新的思维联想。而如今，发表在《细胞报告》上的一项最新研究指出，即便在清醒状态下，人们也有可能进入这种类似梦境的状态。

paragraphs.contentEn: To explore the nether realm between sleep and wakefulness, neuroscientists from the Paris Brain Institute took a page out of Edison’s book. They recruited 92 subjects accustomed to napping and describing their experiences (the very definition of a dream job), to nod off while wearing an EEG net and holding a bottle in one hand. After they were roused from their slumber by the falling bottle, they rated their mental experience for bizarreness, fluidity, spontaneity, and perceived level of wakefulness. Meanwhile, the EEG recorded how deeply into sleep they had ventured.
paragraphs.contentZh: 为了探索介于清醒与睡眠之间的过渡状态，来自巴黎脑科学研究所的神经科学家借鉴了爱迪生的做法。研究团队招募了92名习惯打盹、且能够描述自身体验的受试者（可谓名副其实的梦幻工作），让他们在头戴脑电图（EEG）电极帽的同时，单手握瓶打盹。当瓶子坠落将他们唤醒后，受试者需要对刚才的意识体验进行评分，包括其离奇程度、流畅性、自发性，以及主观上的清醒程度。与此同时，脑电图则会记录下他们当时的睡眠深浅状态。

paragraphs.contentEn: Analyzing the reports revealed the participants’ thoughts clustered around four distinct experiences: fleeting recollections (“an image of my dad crossed my mind”); an alert connection to the surrounding environment (“I was listening to the street sounds”); bizarreness (“I saw images of small aliens”); and a high level of voluntary control (“I was thinking about what I would do tomorrow”).
paragraphs.contentZh: 对这些反馈报告的分析显示，受试者的思维内容大致可归为四种不同的体验：一是短暂浮现的回忆（“我脑海中闪过父亲的画面”）；二是对周围环境的清醒感知（“我当时在听街上的声音”）；三是离奇怪诞的念头（“我看见了小外星人的画面”）；四是较高程度的自主控制（“我在思考明天要做什么”）。

paragraphs.contentEn: These experiences seemed to occur independently of sleep state—and even while the subjects were awake. “This is the major finding of our study. The mental states traditionally associated with dreaming can arise just as well when we are asleep as when we are awake,” study author Nicolas Decat said in a statement. “In other words, the content of our thoughts does not follow the boundaries between waking and sleep! One of our participants, while awake, reported seeing ants crawling on her body against a backdrop of crossword puzzles.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 这些体验似乎并不受睡眠状态的限制——甚至在受试者清醒时也会出现。研究作者尼古拉斯·德卡特在一份声明中指出：“这是我们研究的核心发现。那些通常与做梦相关的意识状态，在人们入睡时可以出现，在清醒时同样也会出现。换句话说，我们的思维内容并不受清醒与睡眠边界的限制！举例来说，一名受试者在清醒状态下报告称，她看到蚂蚁在自己身上爬行，背景则是填字游戏的画面。”

paragraphs.contentEn: An analysis of the EEG data revealed a specific brain signature for strange dreamlike experiences such as this one. Researchers say these kinds of mental phenomena are characterized by reduced connectivity between the brain’s occipital lobe, which generates visual imagery during dreams, and the frontal lobe, which controls executive functions. “This signature may well be the correlate of what we feel in such a state: Lucid reasoning is overtaken by a whirlwind of vivid sensations characteristic of dreams,” Decat said.
paragraphs.contentZh: 对脑电图数据的分析显示，此类离奇的类梦境体验对应着一种特定的脑活动特征。研究人员指出，这类心理现象的典型特征是，负责在梦境中生成视觉图像的大脑枕叶，与负责控制执行功能的额叶之间的神经连接出现了减弱。德卡特表示：“这种脑活动特征，很可能对应着我们在这一状态下的主观感受：清晰的理性思维被梦境所特有的、旋风般鲜活的感官体验所取代。”

paragraphs.contentEn: Sometimes you need to unplug, and sometimes you need to unplug different parts of your brain—it could help you make more creative connections. Even if it doesn’t, it’s a great excuse to give your boss next time you get caught nodding off at work.
paragraphs.contentZh: 有时，你需要让自己暂时断电休息；而有时，则需要让大脑的不同部分暂时断开连接——这或许有助于建立更具创造性的思维连接。退一步说，即便这种方式未必奏效，下次你在工作中打盹被老板撞见，它也不失为一个绝佳的借口。
